fields.rationale: States define surgery either by sweeping 'any tissue cut/altered' language, by enumerating specific instruments and energy modalities, by listing what procedures are excluded from optometric scope, by a flat prohibition, or by a narrow in-office minor-procedure carve-out — five meaningfully distinct legislative approaches.

Invasive procedure means any procedure that involves cutting or otherwise infiltrating human tissue by mechanical means including surgery, laser surgery, ionizing radiation, therapeutic ultrasound, administering medication by injection, or the removal of intraocular foreign bodies.

Surgery includes an invasive procedure using instruments that require closure by suturing, clamping, or other similar devices or a procedure in which the presence or assistance of a nurse anesthetist or an anesthesiologist is required, and also includes laser surgery

A procedure using instruments, including lasers, scalpels, or needles, in which human tissue is cut, burned, vaporized, or otherwise altered by any mechanical means, laser, or ionizing radiation. Includes procedures requiring closing by suturing, clamping, or another device. Does not include a noninvasive procedure to remove a superficial foreign body in the conjunctiva, eyelid, or corneal epithelium that has not perforated the Bowman's membrane.

Ophthalmic surgery is defined as any invasive procedure in which human tissue is cut, ablated, or otherwise penetrated by incision, injection, laser, ultrasound, or other means, in order to: Treat human eye diseases; alter or correct refractive error; or alter or enhance cosmetic appearance.

Surgery is defined by the procedures explicitly excluded from optometric practice, including procedures requiring general anesthesia, corneal procedures, vitreous chamber procedures, retinal procedures, orbital surgery, extraocular muscle surgery, eyelid surgery for malignancies or cosmetic repair, lacrimal system surgery, conjunctivoplasty, pterygium surgery, corneal or scleral incisions, corneal transplants, iris or ciliary body surgery, lens extraction, intraocular implants, vitreous removal, and retinal manipulation.
